extracted.intended_audience: scholars and students in humour studies, television studies, media and cultural studies
extracted.subtask_description: A conceptual, interdisciplinary literature-and-theory oriented overview for analysing controversial or 'taboo' comedy as it appears on television, highlighting recurring themes, tensions, and functions. Intended to frame scholarly study rather than provide empirical coding protocols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appreciation and perceived (un)acceptability of taboo comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: The chapter discusses wider issues such as the appreciation and perceived (un)acceptability of taboo comedy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat public and critical appreciation and questions of acceptability as a central analytic axis — i.e., how audiences and institutions judge controversial humour. (This is stated as a key 'wider issue' in the chapter abstract.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Programming (television scheduling and platform contexts)
rubrics_metrics.description: More specific themes connected to programming are identified as important for the study of taboo comedy on television.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how programming decisions — such as scheduling, channel/platform, and editorial policies — shape the production, distribution, and reception of controversial humour. (Mentioned in the abstract as a focal theme.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation of reality on television
rubrics_metrics.description: The representation of reality on television is named as a specific theme related to taboo comedy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyse how controversial comedy constructs, frames or distorts 'reality' on TV (e.g., through parody, satire, staged 'reality' elements). This element is highlighted alongside programming in the chapter summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Underlying mechanisms and functions of taboo comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: The chapter proposes that humour and television studies can offer insights into the underlying mechanisms and functions of taboo comedy on TV.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate the sociocultural, psychological and communicative functions of taboo humour (why it elicits laughter, what social purposes it serves). The abstract frames this as a primary analytic objective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Central and recurring themes and tensions
rubrics_metrics.description: An overview of some central and recurring themes and tensions emerging from observation of a variety of television shows tackling controversial comedy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map and interrogate recurring tensions (e.g., between humour and offence, satire and propaganda, freedom of expression and censorship) as they appear across shows. The chapter promises such an overview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multidisciplinary frame of reference
rubrics_metrics.description: The chapter aims at offering a multidisciplinary frame of reference for the study of controversial humour in this medium, drawing on both Humour Studies and Television Studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine theoretical and methodological tools from multiple disciplines (media studies, cultural studies, humour theory) when analysing taboo comedy. The abstract explicitly states this as an aim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and variety of television shows
rubrics_metrics.description: The chapter is based on observation of a variety of television shows tackling controversial comedy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure comparative breadth: include diverse program types and formats when identifying themes and tensions. The emphasis on 'variety' is explicitly given in the abstract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humour style and stance (e.g., aggressive humour, progressive stance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Keywords attached to the chapter include 'Humour Style', 'Aggressive Humour', and 'Progressive Stance', indicating attention to different humour styles and ideological stances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attend to differences in humour style (aggressive vs. other forms) and the political/ethical stances embodied by comedic content. These aspects are flagged in the chapter metadata/keywords.
